title: Unverified in a real browser: an unexpected track end now reports a FAILED recording; if a webinar page/tab closing at meeting end ends the tracks before the bot requests stop, a normal end would now be reported as failed
evidence: recorder.js now treats any track 'ended' event while no stop was requested (finishing false) as unexpected: capture-error + capture-stopped failed:true, which the receiver now turns into a failed capture. The old code reported the same event as a clean stop (ISS-T034EXT-002). Tests use fakes (track.end() is synthetic). Whether Chrome fires 'ended' on a captured tab's tracks when the meeting page navigates or closes itself before the controller's stop request is NOT verified.
fix_direction: Exercise once in a live tab-capture session (normal end, tab closed by the meeting, controller stop). If the meeting closing the tab is a normal end, have the receiver (which knows the controller's stop intent) classify it, not the extension.

title: No unit test drives the one-line record-commands.ts onEvent change (capture-stopped failed:true sets captureFailure so the record loop ends early)
evidence: The failure still surfaces at the end through deps.stop() throwing (tested in tab-browser.test.ts), so correctness does not depend on the line; it only shortens the wait. runRecord has no cheap seam to test onEvent in isolation.
fix_direction: Extract onEvent classification to a pure function when record-commands is next touched.

title: Receiver fails OPEN on a capture-stopped whose failed is not exactly boolean true: "true", 1, null, "false" or a missing field all end as a successful stop
evidence: Checker probe through createTabBrowserDeps with a fake extension posting the stop after bytes were received and no prior capture-error: failed=true -> stop() rejects 'Recorder reported a failed stop; media is incomplete', state failed; failed=false, "true", "false", 1, null, and field missing -> stop resolved, state stopped. /event does no schema validation beyond the event name. The shipped recorder.js always sends a boolean and only the token holder can post, so this needs a non-conforming producer: a fail-open default on the data-write path, not a defect reachable from the shipped extension.
fix_direction: Treat capture-stopped as clean only when failed === false; anything else is a failure. Same predicate in record-commands.ts onEvent. Add a table test with the seven values (recorded reproduction).

title: Nothing tests the link that keeps a rejected stop() from reaching finalizeRecording: three record-commands.ts mutations survive the whole record-commands test file
area: packages/meeting-bot/src/capture/record-commands.ts runRecord (finally block `if (backend === "tab") throw e;`, `if (captureFailure) throw`, the new capture-stopped failed:true line)
evidence: Per-mutation byte backup, 250 s timeout, node --test --import tsx src/capture/record-commands.test.ts: M5 delete `if (backend === "tab") throw e;` SURVIVED (a failed stop would be logged and the partial normalised and finalised); M7 delete `if (captureFailure) throw new Error(captureFailure);` SURVIVED; M6 delete the new captureFailure line SURVIVED (early exit only). Files restored, hashes equal HEAD. By code reading the chain is correct today (stop() throws, browser-joiner awaits it, runRecord rethrows, finalize unreachable); it is unguarded. Extends ISS-T034FIX-002.
fix_direction: Make finalize and stop injectable in runRecord (or extract a helper) so a test asserts: rejecting deps.stop for the tab backend means finalize/promote is never called and runRecord rejects.

title: A failed capture is visible only as a non-zero exit, stderr and a status.json on disk: no failure alert, no operation row; a failed partial cannot be finalised by lkb finalize
evidence: onBotEvent routes only reconnect-reload and recovered gaps; capture-error and failed stop are not alerted and the finished notification is simply not sent. runRecord removes .record-state.json in its finally, and finalizeControllerRecording for a status other than stopped/recovered requires that file (Recovery controller binding refused otherwise): code reading, not executed. Nothing scans raw/webinars/*.webm automatically, so a failed partial is never ingested by accident (consumer grep).
fix_direction: Send a failure alert from the capture-error / failed-stop path with reason and partial path; document or add the operator route for a failed-but-complete partial (this also bounds the cost of ISS-T034FIX-001).

title: New record-commands tests for the failed-stop chain are wall-clock dependent and fail most runs on this machine; two of the three killed mutants are killed only by the timing assertion
evidence: Five consecutive foreground runs of `node --test --import tsx src/capture/record-commands.test.ts`: run1 23/22 pass; run2 2 failures; run3 1; run4 1; run5 1 (the 'capture-error ends the record loop promptly' test, and once the 'early capture-stopped failed:true' test), with elapsedAfterStart 6.6-9.7 s against `< 3000`. The fake child sleeps 1000 ms and gives up at 6000 ms. Mutants M6 (new early-exit line removed) and M7 (`if (captureFailure) throw` removed) are killed only by that bound.
fix_direction: Assert behaviour not wall time (loop ended before --until with the reason), or inject a clock/poll and use a bound several times larger than the observed load; keep a non-timing assertion that kills M6/M7.
